sanskrit: तस्माच्छास्त्रं प्रमाणं ते कार्याकार्यव्यवस्थितौ । ज्ञात्वा शास्त्रविधानोक्तं कर्म कर्तुमिहार्हसि ॥
hindiTranslation: अतः तेरे लिये कर्तव्यअकर्तव्यकी व्यवस्थामें शास्त्र ही प्रमाण है  ऐसा जानकर तू इस लोकमें शास्त्रविधिसे नियत कर्तव्य कर्म करनेयोग्य है ॥
englishTranslation: Therefore, scripture is your authority for deciding what should be done and what should not be done. Knowing the duties laid out in scripture, you should act here in the world.
essence: Impulse cannot judge action; a higher standard must.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: Right and wrong action should be judged by scripture, not impulse. Knowing that guidance, a person should do the duty set before them.
simpleInsight: You do not have to invent your own moral compass in the heat of confusion.
detailedMeaning: Arjuna has been overwhelmed by doubt. After exposing the ruin caused by desire and lawless action, Krishna closes the argument by grounding right action in scripture. The point is clear: act, but let higher guidance decide what right action is.
modernRelevance: A new judge, unsure about a hard case, goes back to the law books before ruling. Krishna asks Arjuna to do the same with dharma: know what scripture lays down, then act.
translationLiteral: तस्मात् (therefore) / शास्त्रम् (scripture) / प्रमाणम् (authority) / ते (for you) / कार्य-अकार्य-व्यवस्थितौ (in the arrangement of what should be done and what should not be done) / ज्ञात्वा (having known) / शास्त्र-विधान-उक्तम् (spoken in scriptural rule) / कर्म (action / duty) / कर्तुम् (to do) / इह (here) / अर्हसि (you are fit / should)
insight: Scripture is your authority, Krishna tells Arjuna, for deciding what to do and what to avoid.

quoteVariants.text: Let scripture guide your duty. Then act where you stand.
I need a rule deeper than impulse.
